newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures subside on profit-taking, yen.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures subside on profit-taking, yen.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures gave up their early gains and headed south as the yen strengthened and players took profit following the settlement of May Nikkei options in Friday morning trade.
After making a strong start following the Dow's rise, the lead Nikkei 225 June contract slipped into negative territory, ending the morning 165 points lower at 19,940.
"A lot of people may want to lock in their profits with it being a Friday. And it's hard to predict what the Dow's going to do nowadays," a trader with a Japanese futures house said.

He said comments by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan in a speech late on Thursday could have a dampening effect on Wall Street as players might interpret his words as pointing to further rate hikes.
Greenspan said he expected economic growth to slow later this year and next, but added that the central bank would need to act if that did not prove to be the case.
"I think they are likely to raise rates. There's no sign that the U.S. economy is slowing," the trader said.
He said market participants would move to cash in their gains, at least as an initial knee-jerk reaction.
The June Nikkei was expected to be supported initially at the 19,800 level, 80 points below its morning low, and then at around 19,600, he said.
The May MSCI Taiwan index contract was at 339.3 at 0235 GMT against its opening 341.5 on volume of 470 lots.
